source.public_versification_note: Public 20:45–49 = Hebrew 21:1–5; public 21:1–32 = Hebrew 21:6–37. All other selected labels match. Complete original records, including annotations, are hashed.

key_decisions.decision: Binds public 21:1 to Hebrew 21:6.
Preserves plural sanctuaries and three targets.
Keeps righteous alongside wicked without harmonizing with chapter 18.
Retains repeated pairing and geographic reach.
Keeps recognition and no return to sheath.
Renders broken loins as bodily collapse, literal idiom noted.
Preserves four bodily responses and repeated certainty.
Marks the sword poem.
Keeps Lord without tetragrammaton and doubled sword.
Preserves difficult scepter clause and pronoun ambiguity with note.
Keeps preparation and intended wielder.
Retains shared victims and mourning gesture.
Marks difficult relation to scepter rather than silently replacing the clause.
Preserves doubled/tripled force and encircling weapon.
Keeps gates, hearts, and uncertain rare sword noun in note.
Keeps direct weapon address and both directions.
Retains matching divine gesture and cessation of fury.
Introduces the forked-road sign.
Keeps common starting point and hand-sign idiom as signpost.
Preserves both destinations and fortified status.
Retains three divination methods without replacing teraphim with generic gods.
Keeps repeated rams and full assault sequence.
Leaves oath relationship and he referent open with note.
Preserves repeated remembrance and bodily seizure.
Keeps address and notes profane/slain ambiguity.
Preserves two headpieces and reversals without imposing later offices.
Keeps triple ruin and unnamed claimant with right/judgment ambiguity.
Retains transition to Ammon and returning sword cry.
Keeps sword/personified addressee ambiguity for note.
Keeps sudden return command and origin language.
Preserves fire/breath and destructive craftsmanship.
Keeps disappearance of memory and bodily blood.
